requirement:
Every Rust function carrying a test attribute, `#[test]` or an attribute whose
path ends in `test` such as `#[tokio::test]`, including those in Cargo
integration-test targets, MUST carry a `{test}` reference to a requirement or
named example under {cite}`requirements.references.roles`, in a comment
attached to it or within its body. A test function without one MUST be a
validation error naming its file, line, and name.
rationale:
The implementation meets the requirement. One case the text names has no test, so I judge it a gap.

**Implementation**
- `src/rust_coverage.rs#fn[untested_tests]` is marked `{impl}`.
  - It selects `fn` outline nodes whose attached lines, from the node's `line_start` to its `declaration_line`, match `TEST_ATTRIBUTE`. That regex accepts `#[test]` and any path ending in `test`, such as `#[tokio::test(...)]`. It rejects `#[cfg(test)]` and `#[rstest]`.
  - A test counts as covered when a comment owned by that node carries a `{test}` reference, in inline or closed fenced form, to a non-Term definition. The comment owner comes from the outline's comment-ownership rules.
- `src/rust_coverage.rs#fn[validate_rust_functions]` is marked `{impl}` and does the reporting.
  - It iterates every `.rs` file from `rust_files`, which excludes only `vendor`. This includes the Cargo integration-test targets under `tests/`.
  - It pushes a validation error of the form `{file}:{line}: test function {name} has no {test} reference to a requirement or example`. That names the file, line and name.

**Tests**
- `src/rust_coverage.rs#mod[tests]/fn[test_functions_need_a_test_reference]` is marked `{test}`. It checks these cases:
  - A function with a `{test}` comment is accepted.
  - A bare `#[test]` is flagged.
  - A function with only a `{cite}` is flagged.
  - A `#[tokio::test(flavor=...)]` function with no reference is flagged.
  - A `#[cfg(test)]` function and an `#[rstest]` function are ignored.
  - A test nested in `mod tests` is flagged.
- `tests/coverage.rs#fn[a_test_without_a_test_reference_fails_validation_even_in_mod_tests]` is marked `{test}`. It asserts the exact error string, including file, line and name. It also asserts that the helper in `mod tests` produces no error.

**Gap**
- The text says the reference may be "in a comment attached to it or within its body." Every case in the unit test uses a comment attached before the function. The integration test uses no reference at all. No test shows that a `{test}` reference inside a test function's body satisfies the rule.
- The only body-comment test I found is `body_reference` in `finds_uncited_functions_without_using_enclosing_or_string_references`. It uses an `{impl}` reference and is not marked `{test}` for this requirement.
- This named case rests on the comment-owner logic and has its own boundary, so it needs a test. It has none.

**Confirmation:** the assessments disagreed: the first determination was `true` and an independent second assessment's was `false`. A verifier checked the less favorable `false` determination and found an unacknowledged real gap, so `false` is recorded.

Verification:

**Claimed gap: no test shows that a `{test}` reference within a test function's body satisfies the rule. It is real and not acknowledged.**

- The requirement text accepts a `{test}` reference "in a comment attached to it or within its body". Acceptance by a body comment is therefore a named case that needs its own test.
- `src/rust_coverage.rs#fn[untested_tests]` marks a function as tested when a comment owned by that node carries a `{test}` reference. It has no separate branch for body comments, so the body case depends on the outline's comment-ownership rules.
- `src/rust_coverage.rs#mod[tests]/fn[test_functions_need_a_test_reference]` has only one accepted case: `tested`, whose `{test}` comment sits before the function. The other cases are flagged or ignored: a bare `#[test]`, a `{cite}`-only function, an untested `#[tokio::test(...)]`, `#[cfg(test)]`, `#[rstest]`, and a nested test in `mod tests`. None puts a reference inside a body.
- `tests/coverage.rs#fn[a_test_without_a_test_reference_fails_validation_even_in_mod_tests]` uses no reference at all.
- A search for `{test}`…`requirements.references.coverage.tests` in the sources finds only those two tests, plus the book text. The only body-comment test in the file is `body_reference` in `finds_uncited_functions_without_using_enclosing_or_string_references`. It uses an `{impl}` reference and is not marked `{test}` for this requirement, so it does not verify the body case for a test function.
- No `{fixme}` reference to this requirement appears in the inputs, so the gap is not acknowledged.

**Other points I checked.** I found no other gap.
- The implementation is marked `{impl}` in `untested_tests` and `validate_rust_functions`.
- The attribute matching covers `#[test]` and paths ending in `test`.
- The error message names file, line and name.
- The unit and integration tests cover the rejected cases.

**Unclaimed observation.** `rust_files` includes Cargo integration-test targets under `tests/`, but I did not verify that a test exercises this. I did not rely on it.

text: :::{req} coverage.tests
Every Rust function carrying a test attribute, `#[test]` or an attribute whose
path ends in `test` such as `#[tokio::test]`, including those in Cargo
integration-test targets, MUST carry a `{test}` reference to a requirement or
named example under {cite}`requirements.references.roles`, in a comment
attached to it or within its body. A test function without one MUST be a
validation error naming its file, line, and name.
:::{req} roles

Project text files MAY use the `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` roles with a backtick-delimited full requirement or example name, or with a built-in name under {cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, and MAY use the `{fixme}` role in fenced form. A reference MAY instead be written in fenced form, `:::{role} name` on one line, a body, and a closing fence, following the fence rules of {cite}`requirements.ci.span` and {cite}`requirements.ci.fence_lengths`; the fenced form is the same edge with attached commentary, and the inline form carries none. In a source comment, fence lines MUST be recognized after removing each line's comment delimiters within one comment run under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`, and a fence that does not close within its comment run MUST be a validation error. Each reference is a directed edge between its source and the named definition. A source is a project source item or a requirement or example declaration. The roles MUST mean:
- `{cite}`: the source relies on, supports, or refers to the definition. It is an
edge from the source to the definition.
- `{impl}`: the source implements part of the definition: it makes a decision,
performs a check, produces an output, or handles a case that the definition
specifies. A requirement MAY implement part of another requirement by refining
one of its obligations. Calling code that implements a definition, or
producing a result a caller uses to meet it, MUST NOT by itself count as
implementing it. A check MUST count only if the definition states it, or the
source could not meet one of the definition's obligations without it; source
that checks it is consistent with a definition, such as recognizing a form the
definition specifies in order to decide whether to run other behavior, relies
on that definition and calls for `{cite}`. A requirement stating a convention
for every output of a kind, such as every validation error, is implemented by
the source that carries out the convention as a whole, such as the step that
collects and reports those outputs.
- `{test}`: the source is designed to verify behavior the definition specifies:
a test through its scenario and the assertions about that scenario's outcome,
or a named example through the concrete case it describes.
- `{fixme}`: the source acknowledges a known gap in fulfilling the definition. It
MUST use the fenced form, and its body MUST describe the gap. The body MAY
begin with option lines naming issues that track the gap, one per line, in the
form `:github: <owner>/<repo>#<number>`, such as
`:github: rust-lang/rust#123`. `github` MUST be the only recognized option.
A named `{fixme}` MAY appear only in sources outside the book. Validation MUST report
any other option line, a `:github:` value not in that form, an inline
`{fixme}`, a `{fixme}` in a requirement or example declaration, and a
`{fixme}` whose body, without option lines and comment delimiters, is empty.
An unnamed `{fixme}`, a fence of `:::{fixme}` with no name, MAY appear in any
project text, including a requirement or example body, to tie that place to
the issues it names. It MUST have at least one `:github:` option line and MAY
have a description; it is not a reference edge, acknowledges no gap, needs no
coverage, and does not count as a reference for Rust item coverage. Its
issues are checked under {cite}`requirements.cli.fixme_issues`.
`{impl}`, `{test}`, and `{fixme}` are edges from the definition to the source.
Only requirements and examples are assessed; code is reviewed as part of the
definitions it implements or tests.
```text
{impl}`requirements.references.roles`
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`
{test}`requirements.references.roles`
:::{example} coverage.test_module
A helper function inside `mod tests` has no reference and is read by no record.
`habeas status` does not warn about it. A `#[test]` function in the same module
without a `{test}` reference is still a validation error.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.tests`
